Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Angola enacted Law 22/11 on the Protection of Personal Data on 17 June 2011, making it one of 36 African countries with a Data Protection Act. The law establishes data processing principles (transparency, lawfulness, proportionality, purpose, accuracy), regulates sensitive data (including biometric/genetic data), and requires notification/authorisation by the Data Protection Agency (APD). Angola also ratified the Malabo Convention. A draft amendment to the DPA is in progress to address AI and digital ID.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The Angolan Data Protection Agency (Agência de Proteção de Dados, APD) was formally constituted in 2016 (some sources cite October 2019 as when it became operational) under Law 22/11 to oversee collection and processing of personal data, enforce data protection legislation and apply sanctions. The APD has intensified supervisory activities in recent years and has levied significant financial fines against non-compliant organisations. It is responsible for approving international data transfers and authorising processing of sensitive data.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Under Law 4/09 as originally enacted, national IDs were mandated from age 10. Law 3/21 (2021 amendment) removed the minimum age requirement, making the ID available to all ages including newborns. A November 2025 initiative began issuing ID cards to newborns in Zaire Province. Law 4/09 specifies the first issuance is free for applicants aged 6-11. The enrollment eligibility of 6-10 years (category 3) is supported; with the 2021 amendment opening it to younger ages.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: According to the UN Centre of Excellence for CRVS and the World Bank ID4D Diagnostic (2024), in 2022 approximately 46% of Angolan citizens had an ID card (BI). The Paradigm Initiative policy brief (2024) notes 14 million out of 33 million Angolans (approximately 42%) hold an identity card. The World Bank 2017 data cited 28% biometric national ID coverage. Birth registration stands at 77% (2022 UN data). The 46% BI coverage places Angola in the 20-49% range.
